messages:
claire (People Ops): Heads up  odd benefits case. Employee was terminated 2025-04-15, took a partial 401(k) distribution and a loan offset on 2025-04-30. They were rehired 2025-09-01 and re-enrolled in benefits. We also changed 401(k) recordkeeper (vendor cutover) on 2025-06-15 while they were off payroll. Employee asks: can they roll their distribution back / do a rollover-in given the cutover? Can we restore loan status or re-establish loan repayment? And is there any employer match or rehire catch-up treatment for the pre-termination wages? Any vendor/legal blockers?
ben (Payroll): Dates are super helpful  thanks. Quick answers depend on (1) whether distribution was direct to employee or a trustee-to-trustee rollover, (2) whether they are within the 60-day rollover window, and (3) if the legacy recordkeeper has final custody. Do you have the distribution check date and whether employee elected direct rollover? Also need their legacy plan participant id.
claire (People Ops): Distribution check date 2025-04-30, it was paid to employee (not a direct rollover). They contacted us on 2025-05-10 asking about rollover but by then the cutover was already scheduled and recordkeeping contact was in flux. They were rehired 2025-09-01 and want to put the money back if possible. Legacy participant id: LP-77821.
max (Finance): From an accounting/tax perspective: if they repaid/rolled in within 60 days we can treat it as a rollover and it's not taxable. If past 60 days, it's a taxable distribution and any loan offset is treated as distribution (potentially subject to income/penalties if under age). Employer match for pre-termination deferrals  match is based on elective deferrals actually remitted before termination. If deferrals were remitted prior to 04/15 we owe match for those pay periods; if not, there's nothing to match. We also need to reconcile records across the two vendors for matching.
alex (Employee): Hi team 1: I got the cash and deposited it. I had planned to roll it back but then we had the vendor switch and I got worried about timelines. Is there anything I can sign now to make this easier? I do want to re-contribute if allowed.
amira (Legal): High-level: IRS 60-day rollover rule applies for indirect rollovers (employee received distribution). Plan document may permit a rollover in within 60 days, but plan admin/recordkeeper must accept a rollover-in. After a recordkeeper cutover there are two custody records; we need legacy vendor to confirm ability to accept incoming rollover or route funds to new vendor. Also, loan offsets are generally treated as distributions; some plans allow recontribution of offset amounts as rollover if done within 60 days, others do not. We'll need to review the plan document and any distribution paperwork the employee signed (e.g., attestation they weren't going to rollover).
ben (Payroll): Vendor note: legacy recordkeeper still processes rollovers/rollins for distributions taken prior to cutover, but they require a copy of the distribution check stub, participant id, and a rollover-in instruction. After cutover there's an added reconciliation step to map funds to the new urn. We can open a vendor reconciliation ticket but acceptance is not guaranteed. If the 60-day window has passed, legal/finance will need to coordinate tax reporting.
benefits-bot: Policy excerpt: "Indirect distributions (payable to the participant) may be rolled over within 60 days if the plan and recordkeeper accept roll-in contributions. Loan offsets are generally treated as taxable distributions unless rolled over per IRS rules and plan doc. For recordkeeper cutovers, submit docs to payroll@redwood for reconciliation: distribution stub, participant id, signed rollover instruction, and proof of 60-day timing." <https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/401k-rollover-policy>
max (Finance): Action items from finance side: if a rollover-in is possible we need written confirmation from legacy vendor, a remittance instruction, and to know whether the funds will land in the legacy plan or be pushed to the new recordkeeper. If funds are taxable we'll need to prepare W-2 adjustments and the appropriate 1099-R (depending on timing).
claire (People Ops): Next steps I propose: 1) ask employee to confirm whether they deposited the check and the deposit date, 2) collect distribution stub + signed distribution election paperwork, 3) payroll to open vendor recon ticket asking legacy vendor to accept rollover-in and confirm mapping to new vendor, 4) legal to review plan doc for loan-offset rollover allowance. Ben  can you open the vendor ticket? Amira  can you start plan doc review?
ben (Payroll): Will open vendor ticket today (ref: TKT-401K-ROLL-2135) and request legacy vendor acceptance and 60-day viability. Please DM me the distribution stub and deposit date rather than posting in channel.
amira (Legal): I'll pull the plan doc and distribution paperwork tonight and flag language about loan offsets and indirect rollovers. If we find a prohibition we'll advise employee on tax consequences and any corrective options.
alex (Employee): Deposit date was 2025-05-02. I have the distribution paperwork scanned. I'll DM the files now. Thanks for taking a look.
claire (People Ops): Great  I'll DM Ben the stub and Alex  please CC me on the DM so I can track. I'll also confirm whether company match for pre-termination wages is already reconciled or needs a manual remit.
ben (Payroll): A note on employer match: even if distribution occurred, employer match for prior deferrals is still owed if deferrals were remitted. But if the payroll export shows no deferrals recorded before 04/15 then there's nothing to match. We'll reconcile and advise.
max (Finance): We'll hold a provisional PO for any manual match remittance until vendor confirms. If taxable distribution is unavoidable, finance/legal will coordinate communications and tax forms.
claire (People Ops): Thanks team. I'll update here once vendor responds. If legacy vendor can accept a rollover-in we'll coordinate next steps with Alex.
